finding_1.claim: Adyen operates a common backend spanning multiple payment functions.
finding_1.reason: The claim is bounded and descriptive. E-012 supports the architecture observation, while the issuer-origin limitation is kept as a qualification rather than inverted into counterevidence.

finding_2.claim: Enterprise customers can shift payment volume away from Adyen or replace it as a provider.
finding_2.reason: The claim is framed directly at substitution and volume-migration capability, so E-037/E-041/E-051 now support the exact skeptical proposition instead of being misclassified as counterevidence to low churn. C-005 remains a broader switching-friction tension rather than false counterevidence.

finding_3.claim: Adyen reports payment-optimization improvements across conversion, authorization, and cost metrics.
finding_3.reason: Reported outcomes are directionally supported and issuer/denominator limitations remain orthogonal qualifications.

low_reported_churn_false_counterevidence.interpretation: The model did not repeat the v0.9 low-churn error. Instead it framed E-037/E-041/E-051 as support for a substitution-capability claim and moved the low-churn versus multi-provider tension to the switching-friction weak link.

switching_friction_same_target.interpretation: The weak-link candidate combines E-036, E-037 and E-041 around switching friction coherently, but no priority finding used same-target support plus counterevidence, so the MIXED/counterevidence path is not directly proven.

service_disruption_scope_regression.interpretation: E-055/E-056 were not selected in the three priority findings, so the v0.9 false-counterevidence regression for incident existence was not re-tested by this execution.

e040_orthogonal_qualification.interpretation: E-040 appears in weak-link and unresolved-point grounding only. No directional SUPPORT-plus-qualification regression was exercised.

e043_support_direction.interpretation: E-043 appears only in an unresolved question and is not assigned a directional evidence role.

weak_link_label.interpretation: Short weak-link labels remain valid without terminal punctuation.

positive_evidence: No generated priority finding contains the v0.9 claim-target polarity errors.
The model selected a skeptical substitution-capability claim for E-037/E-041/E-051 instead of attaching those items as counterevidence to a low-churn observation.
Qualifications remained orthogonal to evidence direction.
Switching friction is represented as an uncertainty/weak-link question rather than collapsed into a misleading descriptive finding.
remaining_uncertainty: No priority finding contained counterevidence_ids, so same-target counterevidence assignment was not directly exercised.
No priority finding used MIXED status, so the MIXED semantic-target rule was not directly exercised.
The E-055/E-056 service-incident scope regression was not exercised.
E-040 and E-043 directional regression targets were not exercised as priority findings.
contract_learning.conclusion: v1.0 materially improves observed Adyen behavior and yields a human-quality-admissible output, but this single stochastic canary is insufficient to freeze claim-target alignment because several targeted regression paths were not exercised.

spend.note: No post-call rounded budget snapshot is required for this result because no further paid execution is authorized by this artifact.

stop_rule.reason: The v1.0 canary is a human-quality-admissible observation but does not fully exercise the targeted counterevidence/MIXED and service-scope regression paths. Stop and design the next calibration step before any additional paid call.
